mainTopic: Replacing a disqualified כהן גדול, and how רבי יהודה's backup wife for יום הכיפורים could work
overview: The עמוד opens by ruling like רבי יוסי about a replacement כהן גדול. The replacement does not serve once the original is fit again, but his service counts if he served anyway, and he takes over if the original dies. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's dispute about preparing a backup wife. The רבנן prepare a backup כהן but not a backup wife, because טומאה is common and death is not, and the כהן גדול is careful about impurity. רבי יהודה says one death is a real worry but two are not. The גמרא then asks how רבי יהודה's backup wife could even work, since the Torah requires the כהן גדול to have exactly one wife ('ביתו') on יום הכיפורים. It tries betrothal, full marriage, and several conditional גיטין, and each one leaves him with no wife or with two. Along the way it uses רבא's rule that a condition tying husband and wife together for life is not כריתות. The final attempt, a גט on condition that the other wife does not die, is challenged at the end of the עמוד, and that challenge continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, and service done anyway is valid
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is like רבי יוסי, but he agrees that the replacement כהן גדול's service is valid after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי. And רבי יוסי agrees that if the replacement priest went ahead and served, his service is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules like רבי יוסי from the ברייתא on the previous עמוד. It adds that he agrees the replacement's service still counts if he served anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי held that the replacement may not serve as כהן גדול, because that would cause איבה (hatred) between him and the original. Serving as a כהן הדיוט is also not allowed, because מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין. Since the ban is only to avoid hatred, it does not remove his status, so his service after the fact is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of
Went ahead and served against the rule (after the fact)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוסי says the replacement is no longer a כהן גדול at all. He keeps that status; he is only told not to serve because of איבה. That is why his service counts after the fact.

phrases.english: The halacha is like Rabbi Yosei,
and Rabbi Yosei agrees
that if he went ahead and served —
his service is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי from the ברייתא on the previous עמוד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, but if the replacement כהן גדול served anyway, his service is valid.

steps.title: If the original כהן גדול dies, the replacement takes over
steps.stepSummary: רב adds that רבי יוסי agrees the replacement becomes כהן גדול once the original dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, and רבי יוסי agrees that if the first כהן גדול died, the replacement returns to his service.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה, quoting רב, gives a second point that רבי יוסי concedes. If the original כהן גדול dies, the replacement may serve as כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on the replacement serving was only to prevent hatred with the original. Once the original has died, there is no one left to resent him, so he can serve.

keyTerms.meaning: רב יהודה said in the name of his teacher, רב
Returns to his service (as כהן גדול)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
The halacha is like Rabbi Yosei,
and Rabbi Yosei agrees
that if the first one died,
that he (the replacement) returns to his service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second concession by רבי יוסי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the original כהן גדול dies, the replacement serves as כהן גדול.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed to say this at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's statement as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason to keep the replacement out was hatred with the original. If the original is dead, that reason is clearly gone, so why state it?

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new)

phrases.english: That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב's statement
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that the replacement returns after the original dies
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason for the ban (איבה) disappears when the original dies, so the ruling seems self-evident.

steps.title: We might have thought it is like a rival wife
steps.stepSummary: Without רב's statement, one might have compared the replacement to a צרה taken during the first wife's lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: he is like a rival wife taken during the lifetime of the first. So רב teaches us that this is not a concern.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב's statement does teach something new. It rejects a reason we might have had to keep the replacement out even after the original's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צרה (rival wife) married while the first wife is still alive causes lasting resentment. Here, the replacement already stood waiting to take over while the original was alive. One might think that alone keeps him barred even after death; רב teaches that it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
He teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

phrases.english: You might have said,
it is for him like a rival wife from (the first's) lifetime.
He teaches us (otherwise).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא, showing a real חידוש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the replacement was a 'rival' during the original's lifetime, perhaps he stays barred even after death.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the original dies, there is no concern, and the replacement serves as כהן גדול.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי. The replacement does not serve while the original is fit, but his service counts after the fact. If the original dies, he becomes כהן גדול.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: רבי יהודה wants a backup wife too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's view in the משנה that a backup wife is also prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: They even prepare another wife for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the opening משנה of the מסכת and quotes רבי יהודה. This sets up a discussion of the רבנן's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the כהן גדול atones 'for himself and for his household' (ביתו), and ביתו means his wife. If she dies before יום הכיפורים, he would have no 'household', so רבי יהודה says to prepare a second wife.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
They even prepare another wife for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף אִשָּׁה אַחֶרֶת מַתְקִינִין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the replacement כהן to the backup-wife dispute in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a backup wife is prepared for the כהן גדול in case his wife dies.

steps.title: Don't the רבנן also worry about 'maybe'?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן worry that the כהן גדול may become impure, so why not that his wife may die?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן too, don't they worry about 'maybe'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the רבנן, who reject a backup wife. They do prepare a backup כהן in case of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן accept preparing a backup כהן in case the כהן גדול becomes impure. That shows they worry about possible problems, so their refusal to worry about the wife's death looks inconsistent.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis too,
don't they worry about 'perhaps'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבנן's rejection of רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's refusal to prepare a backup wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: They worry about טומאה (backup כהן), so they should also worry about death (backup wife).

steps.title: Impurity is common, death is not
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן distinguish: טומאה happens often, death rarely.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן would tell you: טומאה is common; death is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the רבנן. They only plan for problems that happen often.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול can easily become טמא, from his own body or from outside contact. Death of his wife within a short window is rare, so the רבנן do not prepare for it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis would tell you:
impurity is common,
death is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against the רבנן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (common vs. uncommon risk)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן seem to worry about טומאה but not about death, which looks inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: We only prepare for common risks; טומאה is common, death is not.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: 'If so, there is no end'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the רבנן's objection to רבי יהודה in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If so, there is no end to the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the רבנן's reply to רבי יהודה from the משנה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן argue that if we worry the first wife might die, we must also worry the second might die, then the third, and so on forever.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no end to the matter

phrases.english: They said to him:
If so, there is no end to the matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם כֵּן, אֵין לַדָּבָר סוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן reject a backup wife because the worry would never end.

steps.title: The Rabbis made a good point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes the רבנן's argument is strong, implying רבי יהודה needs an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They spoke well to רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the רבנן's argument seems convincing. This is really a challenge to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'no end' logic looks airtight. If one death is a worry, two should be too, so how can רבי יהודה stop at one backup wife?

phrases.aramaic: שַׁפִּיר קָא אָמְרִי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה!
phrases.english: They are speaking well to Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָא אָמְרִי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Endorses the רבנן's argument, putting pressure on רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's requirement of one backup wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first wife's death is a worry, the second's should be too, so there is no logical stopping point.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: one death we worry about, two we don't
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה draws a line: one death is a reasonable worry, two deaths are too unlikely.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה would tell you: for the death of one, we worry; for the death of two, we don't worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's defense. He explains where the worry stops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that one wife dying is possible enough to plan for. Two wives both dying in that short period is so unlikely that we ignore it. So the chain stops after one backup.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda — he would tell you:
for the death of one — we are concerned.
For the death of two — we are not concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יהודה against the 'no end' argument
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setting a limit on the concern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Worrying about one death logically requires worrying about endless deaths.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one death is a realistic worry; two deaths are too unlikely to consider.

steps.title: How would the רבנן respond?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן would say to רבי יהודה's limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? (What would they say?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן would answer רבי יהודה's distinction. This sets up their reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's limit seems reasonable. The גמרא wants to know why the רבנן still reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Rabbis? (i.e., how would they respond?)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the רבנן's counter-response
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן would respond to רבי יהודה's one-but-not-two distinction

steps.title: The רבנן: if we worry at all, we worry even for two
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject the limit: once death is a concern, two deaths must be one too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is reason to worry, then even for the death of two we would worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's reply. They do not accept a halfway point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, either death is too rare to worry about at all, as they hold, or it is a real concern. If it is a real concern, there is no reason to stop after one. So the 'no end' argument stands, and they prepare no backup wife.

keyTerms.meaning: If there is reason to be concerned

phrases.english: If there is reason to be concerned —
even for the death of two we would be concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how the רבנן respond
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If death is worth worrying about at all, we would worry even about two deaths, so there is no stopping point.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה worries about one wife dying but not two. The רבנן say death is not common, and if it were a real worry, there would be no stopping point. So the רבנן prepare a backup כהן but not a backup wife.

steps.title: Turning the רבנן's logic back on them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the רבנן: if worrying about one death means worrying about two, then worrying about one impurity should mean worrying about two impurities.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, let them say this about themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the רבנן's own rule ('if you worry about one, worry about two') and applies it to their own ruling about a backup כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree that we appoint a backup כהן גדול in case the real one becomes impure. By their own logic, we should also worry that the backup becomes impure. Then we would need a second backup, and the chain would never end.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority opinion in the משנה)
To themselves / about their own position

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, let them say it about themselves!
phrases.notes: Meaning: apply your 'two is like one' logic to the backup כהן גדול too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the רבנן's answer from Step 12 as a weapon against their own ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's ruling to appoint only one backup כהן גדול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the רבנן's own reasoning, if a risk is worth worrying about once, it is worth worrying about twice. Since they worry about impurity, they should also worry that the backup becomes impure, which would require a second backup priest.

steps.title: The כהן גדול is careful
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that a כהן גדול is careful about impurity, so a second backup is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן can say to you: the כהן גדול is careful.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן explain why impurity is different from death: a כהן גדול works hard to avoid becoming impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not worry about death at all, because it is not common (Step 7); they only said that if one did worry, being careful cannot prevent death, so there would be no reason to stop at one. Impurity is different, because a כהן גדול can avoid it by being careful. So one backup כהן is enough, and the 'no end' chain never starts.

keyTerms.meaning: They can say to you (introduces a defense)

phrases.english: The Rabbis can say to you:
The High Priest is vigilant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases (impurity can be avoided; death cannot)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Worrying about impurity should work just like worrying about death.
steps.terutzMaskana: A careful כהן גדול makes a second impurity too unlikely to plan for.

steps.title: Then why have any backup at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן גדול is careful, why appoint even one backup?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is careful, why do they prepare another כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the 'he is careful' argument seems to prove too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If carefulness is enough to protect him, the first backup should not be needed either. But the משנה clearly says a backup is appointed.

phrases.english: If he is vigilant,
why do they designate another priest?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי זָרִיז הוּא, לָמָּה מַתְקִינִין כֹּהֵן אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the כהן גדול's carefulness makes worry unnecessary
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If carefulness removes the worry, even the first backup becomes pointless.

steps.title: A rival makes him even more careful
steps.stepSummary: The backup is appointed as a 'rival', and this pushes the כהן גדול to be even more careful.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since we make a rival for him, all the more so he will be extra careful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the backup is partly there to motivate the כהן גדול, not only to replace him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול does not want to lose his special day to someone else. Seeing a rival standing ready makes him guard himself even more. So one backup is useful, and a second one is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A rival (like a co-wife; here, a competing priest)

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן appoint one backup כהן גדול. A second is not needed because the כהן גדול is careful, and the rival makes him more careful still. Death cannot be prevented by being careful, so for the רבנן a worry about death would have no stopping point. That is why they prepare no backup wife at all, but do prepare one backup כהן.

phrases.english: Since we create a rival for him,
all the more so he will be more vigilant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 and closes the discussion about the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the purpose of the backup
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The backup exists only in case the כהן גדול becomes impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The backup also motivates the כהן גדול to be extra careful.

steps.title: A backup woman is not 'his house'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: merely designating a woman does not make her 'ביתו', his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is preparing her enough? The Torah said 'ביתו', and this woman is not his house!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against רבי יהודה's idea of preparing a backup wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול must atone 'for his house', which means his wife. A woman who has only been chosen, but not married to him, is not his wife. So choosing her does not solve the problem if his wife dies.

phrases.english: And is designation sufficient for him?
The Merciful One said 'his house,'
and this one is not his house!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבנן's position and challenges how רבי יהודה's backup wife would actually work.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling to prepare a backup wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse requires an actual wife. A woman who is only designated is not his wife.

steps.title: He betroths her
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he does קידושין with the backup woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: He betroths her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the backup woman is not merely chosen; he gives her קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידושין creates a real marriage bond. The hope is that this makes her count as his wife.

phrases.english: That he betroths her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The backup woman is only designated.

steps.title: Betrothal is not yet 'his house'
steps.stepSummary: Before נישואין, she is still not called his 'house'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But as long as he has not married her fully, she is not his house!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that קידושין alone is not enough to make her 'ביתו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His house' means a wife living with him, and that requires נישואין (full marriage). A woman who only has קידושין does not qualify yet.

phrases.english: But as long as he has not married her —
she is not his house!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that קידושין makes her his wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'ביתו' requires full marriage, not only betrothal.

steps.title: He fully marries her
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he does נישואין with the backup woman too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He marries her fully.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he completes the marriage with the second woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now she is fully his wife, so she clearly counts as 'ביתו'.

keyTerms.meaning: Full marriage (the second stage after קידושין)

phrases.english: That he marries her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19.

steps.title: Now he has two houses
steps.stepSummary: If both women are his wives, he has two houses, but the Torah says one house.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he has two houses, and the Torah said 'he shall atone for himself and for his house' — not for two houses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that fully marrying the second woman creates the opposite problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse uses the singular, 'his house'. That means one wife, not two. So a כהן גדול with two wives does not fit the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall atone for himself and for his house' (ויקרא טז)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the trap the גמרא is building. He needs exactly one wife on יום כפורים: zero wives is a problem, and two wives is also a problem.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, הָוֵה לֵיהּ שְׁנֵי בָתִּים,
phrases.english: If so, he has two houses,
and the Merciful One said:
'And he shall atone for himself and for his house,'
and not for two houses!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, הָוֵה לֵיהּ שְׁנֵי בָתִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that he fully marries the second woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two full wives go against the singular 'ביתו' in the verse.

steps.title: He then divorces her
steps.stepSummary: The answer: after marrying the second woman, he divorces her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then divorces her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests he divorces the second woman, so he is left with only one wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Divorcing her removes the 'two houses' problem.

phrases.english: That he then divorces her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both women stay married to him.

steps.title: Back to the original problem
steps.stepSummary: If he divorces her, she is not his wife, and we are back at the first question.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he divorces her, our difficulty returns to its place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that divorce brings back the problem from Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she is divorced, she cannot step in if the first wife dies. The whole backup plan becomes useless again.

keyTerms.meaning: Our difficulty returns to its place

phrases.english: If he divorces her,
our difficulty returns to its place!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מְגָרֵשׁ לַהּ, הָדְרָא קוּשְׁיַין לְדוּכְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 22 by bringing back the challenge of Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that he divorces the second woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A divorced woman is not 'ביתו', so she cannot serve as a backup.

steps.title: A conditional divorce: 'on condition that you die'
steps.stepSummary: He gives her a גט on condition that she dies, so the divorce only works if she actually dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he divorces her with a condition, saying to her: 'This is your גט on condition that you die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a clever conditional גט, so that he always ends up with exactly one wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she dies on יום כפורים, the גט takes effect backward, and the other wife was his only wife. If she does not die but the other wife dies, the גט never takes effect, and she remains his one wife. Either way, he has one house.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (introduces a narrowed case)

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where he divorces her on condition.
That he says to her:
This is your bill of divorce on condition that you die.
phrases.notes: This square bracket opens a stretch of words that some versions don't have. It closes a few lines on, at the next 'על מנת'.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דִּמְגָרֵשׁ לַהּ עַל תְּנַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 with a conditional divorce.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a conditional divorce
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The divorce is a complete, ordinary divorce.
steps.terutzMaskana: The divorce depends on whether she dies, so he always has one wife.

steps.title: What if nobody dies?
steps.stepSummary: If neither woman dies, the גט never takes effect, and he has two wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps she will not die, and he will have two houses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a hole in the 'on condition that you die' plan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The most likely outcome is that no one dies. Then the condition is never met, the גט never works, and he is married to both women. That brings back the 'two houses' problem of Step 21.

phrases.english: But perhaps she will not die,
and he will have two houses!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conditional גט of Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'on condition that you die' גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no one dies, the גט never takes effect, leaving two wives.

steps.title: Flip the condition: 'on condition that you do not die'
steps.stepSummary: He gives the גט on condition that she does not die. If she lives, she is divorced; if she dies, the other wife remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he says to her: 'This is your גט on condition that you do not die.' If she does not die, she is divorced. If she dies, the other one is still there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the condition to fix the 'two houses' problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now, if she lives, the גט works, and he has only the other wife. If she dies, the other wife still stands as his one wife. This avoids having two wives in the normal case.

phrases.english: Rather, where he says to her:
This is your bill of divorce on condition
phrases.notes: This bracket closes the section that opened back in Step 24.

phrases.english: that you will not die.
If she does not die — she is divorced.
And if she dies, behold — the other one remains.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאָמַר לַהּ: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטֵּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁלֹּא תָּמוּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed condition of Step 24 with the opposite condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition is 'that you do not die', so in the normal case he has one wife.

steps.title: He might be left with no wife
steps.stepSummary: If she lives, her גט is valid, and if the other wife dies, he is left with no wife at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps she will not die, so her גט is a real גט, and her fellow wife will die, and he is left without a house!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a new hole: the flipped condition can leave him with zero wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture the case where the divorced woman lives and the other wife dies. The גט has already taken effect, and his only remaining wife has died. So he has no 'ביתו', which is exactly what רבי יהודה was trying to prevent.

keyTerms.meaning: Without a house — without a wife
This גט is a valid גט

steps.whyThisMatters: Each fix created a new problem: no wife, then two wives, then no wife again. This shows how hard it is to guarantee exactly one wife on יום כפורים. The גמרא continues working on this problem later.

phrases.english: But perhaps she does not die,
and her bill of divorce is a valid bill of divorce,
and her counterpart dies,
and he is left without a house!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the flipped condition of Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'on condition that you do not die' גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she lives and the other wife dies, the valid גט leaves him with no wife.

steps.title: A divorce tied to one of the wives dying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests he gives the גט on condition that one of the two wives dies, so whichever survives is his one wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he says to her: 'on condition that one of you dies.' If this one dies, that one remains. If that one dies, this one remains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to set up the condition so the כהן גדול always ends up with exactly one wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The divorce now depends on one of the two women dying. Whichever woman is still alive is his wife, so he is never left with zero wives.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, דְּאָמַר לַהּ: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתָּמוּת [אַחַת מִכֶּם].
phrases.english: Rather, he says to her: on condition that one of you dies.
If this one dies, that one remains;
if that one dies, doesn't this one remain?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּאָמַר לַהּ: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתָּמוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the condition that failed in step 27 with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rephrasing the condition of the גט
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every earlier condition left him with two wives or with none.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tying the גט to one of them dying guarantees one surviving wife.

steps.title: What if neither wife dies?
steps.stepSummary: If neither woman dies, the condition is never met, and he has two wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe neither one of them dies, and he will have two houses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new condition: it only works if someone actually dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually both women stay alive. Then the condition 'one of you dies' never happens, the גט never takes effect, and the כהן גדול has two wives. The Torah's 'his house' (ביתו) means only one.

phrases.aramaic: וְדִילְמָא לָא מָיְיתָא וְלָא חֲדָא מִינַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: But perhaps not even one of them dies,
and he will have two houses?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא לָא מָיְיתָא וְלָא חֲדָא מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 28.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The likely outcome, nobody dies, leaves him with two wives.

steps.title: Is such a divorce even valid?
steps.stepSummary: A second problem: a גט with this kind of condition may not count as a גט at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: is something like this a valid גט?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second, deeper problem with the condition. It is setting up a proof from רבא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 said the condition might never be met. Now the גמרא asks whether a condition tied to the couple's own lives can work at all. If it cannot, the plan fails even when someone dies.

phrases.english: And furthermore: in a case like this,
is it a valid bill of divorce?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: כִּי הַאי גַּוְונָא מִי הָוֵי גִּיטָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge against the step 28 תירוץ.
steps.kashyaTarget: The validity of a גט with a condition tied to the wives' lives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט must fully cut the bond. A condition linked to her own life may keep them connected.

steps.title: רבא's rule about conditions that do not cut the bond
steps.stepSummary: רבא: a condition lasting 'all the days of my life and your life' is not כריתות, but one tied to a third person's life is.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא said: 'Here is your גט on condition that you do not drink wine all the days of my life and your life' is not severance. 'All the days of the life of so-and-so' is severance!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's ruling to prove the challenge of step 30.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls a גט a 'ספר כריתות', a document of cutting off. A condition that binds her for as long as she or her husband lives keeps them linked forever, so it is not a real cut. A condition tied to an outsider's life is fine. A condition tied to the wives' own lives works like the first case, so it fails.

keyTerms.meaning: severance, a full cutting of the marriage bond
all the days of my life and your life

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not reject conditions in a גט. Most conditions are fine. Only a condition that keeps husband and wife tied to each other for life fails as כריתות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains why the next answer ties the גט to the OTHER wife's life, which counts like a third person ('פלוני').

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
'This is your bill of divorce on condition
that you will not drink wine

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יְמֵי חַיַּי וְחַיַּיְכִי״ — אֵין זֶה כְּרִיתוּת.
phrases.english: all the days of my life and your life': that is not severance.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יְמֵי חַיַּי פְּלוֹנִי — הֲרֵי זֶה כְּרִיתוּת!
phrases.english: 'All the days of the life of so-and-so': that is severance!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the challenge in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: A condition tied to the couple's own lives makes the גט invalid
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling on 'all the days of my life and your life' compared with 'the life of so-and-so'

steps.title: A divorce on condition that the other wife does not die
steps.stepSummary: He tells the second wife: 'Here is your גט on condition that your fellow wife does not die.' If the first wife lives, the second is divorced. If the first dies, the second stays married.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he says to her: 'Here is your גט on condition that your fellow wife does not die.' If her fellow wife does not die, she is divorced. If that one dies, this one remains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new condition that fixes both problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition now depends on the OTHER woman's life, which is like 'פלוני' in רבא's rule, so it is real כריתות. If the first wife lives, the second is divorced and he has one wife. If the first dies, the second's גט fails and she is his one wife.

phrases.english: Rather, he says to her:
This is your bill of divorce on condition
that your fellow wife does not die.
If her fellow wife does not die, she is divorced;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי מָיְתָה הָא — הָא קָיְימָא הָא.
phrases.english: and if that one dies, doesn't this one remain?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּאָמַר לַהּ: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטֵּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁלֹּא תָּמוּת חֲבֶרְתִּיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both challenges (steps 29 and 31) with a new condition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tying the condition to a third party's life
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A condition tied to 'one of you dying' fails, either in practice or as כריתות.
steps.terutzMaskana: A condition tied to the other wife living always leaves one wife and counts as real כריתות.

steps.title: What if the other wife dies in the middle of the service?
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the first wife dies partway through the יום כפורים עבודה, and it then becomes clear that something went wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps her fellow wife dies in the middle of the service, and the matter becomes clear...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new challenge to the latest answer. The sentence continues into the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first wife dies during the עבודה, the second wife's condition turns out to have failed. That reveals that the second wife was never divorced. So for the part of the service already done, he really had two wives. The rest of the argument comes on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: in the middle of the (יום כפורים) service

steps.confusionAlert: This קשיא is not finished here. The words 'ואיגלי מלתא' lead into the conclusion on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: But perhaps her fellow wife dies
in the middle of the service,
and the matter becomes revealed

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The condition 'your fellow wife does not die'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A death partway through the service reveals that the second wife was never divorced, so he had two wives during part of the עבודה.
